newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders target EU wheat refund of 16.50 Ecus.
newsitem.headline: Traders target EU wheat refund of 16.50 Ecus.

text.p: Grain exporters on Thursday said they expected the European Union to grant a refund of 16.50 Ecus per tonne on soft wheat exports at this week's tender.
Based on bids, this would clear the release of up to 215,000 tonnes of wheat in France, plus any additional exports granted elsewhere in the European Union, they said.
In France grain traders bid to export 952,500 tonnes of EU soft wheat at refunds ranging from 15.67 to 21.47 Ecus a tonne.
Traders also bid to export 22,000 tonnes of free market wheat in Germany, 38,500 in Austria and 42,000 tonnes in Sweden, exporters said.
Last week the EU granted the export of 115,500 tonnes of soft wheat at a refund of 17.99 Ecus per tonne.
Exporters said that a firmer dollar allowed the EU to reduce the wheat export refund this week.
"The EU can easily give 200,000 tonnes and at a good discount over last week," one exporter said.
On Wednesday EU farm director general Guy Legras said the wheat rebate level awarded at this week's auction would depend on the world market price and the value of the dollar.
"If the dollar goes up, the refund goes down," Legras said.
The lowest bid for wheat subsidy placed in France was for the export of 100,000 tonnes of soft wheat, exporters said.

Other cumulative offers included bids to export up to 215,000 tonnes of wheat at a refund of 16.50 Ecus, up to 382,000 tonnes at 17.00, 481,000 tonnes at 17.50, 743,000 tonnes at 18.00 Ecus and up to 952,500 tonnes at 21.47 Ecus.
In France exporters said a rebate of 15.67 Ecus was aggressive because it valued French wheat at around $146 per tonne, some $6 above a recent sale of French wheat to Iran.
Exporters linked the large tonnage sought this week partly to recent business with Egypt and Iran but also to sustained business with eastern Europe.
They estimated the export licence short at more than one million tonnes.
Rouen wheat for March delivery was quoted steady at 865 francs per tonne on Thursday.
